info.title: Agilis Advertising REST API: Webhooks
info.summary: Manage the endpoints Agilis sends events to, send test events, and list and resend webhook events.
info.description:
Return codes are in the JSON body (`return_code`). They are scoped to the endpoint: the same code can mean different things on different endpoints, so read each operation's `x-return-codes`.

Rate limits: 60 requests a minute per API key, uploads included. Responses carry `X-RateLimit-Limit` and `X-RateLimit-Remaining`; over the limit the API returns 429 with `Retry-After`. Repeated requests with an invalid key are refused for a while with 429 and `Retry-After`. Every bad key returns the same 401 Unauthorised. TEST Offers and Events are deleted 30 days after they end.

Human-readable reference: https://www.agilis.dating/api-doc · Markdown: https://www.agilis.dating/api-doc.md

servers.description: Production. TEST or LIVE is chosen by the API key (pk_test_ / pk_live_) and the environment parameter.

get.description: Your organisation's webhook endpoints in your key's mode. The signing secret is never returned here: it is shown only when the endpoint is created and when its secret is rolled. Org Admin and Developer API keys only; an Advertiser's key is refused (HTTP 403, `E2`). Endpoints belong to the organisation and to your key's mode: a TEST key sees TEST endpoints only.

200.description: S1: Endpoints returned (up to 16).

401.description: Invalid or missing API key, or a disabled account. Every bad key gets the same 401.

403.description: E2: The key is not an Org Admin's or a Developer's.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (60 requests a minute per API key, or repeated invalid keys): wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait. Sent when the per-key limit or the invalid-key limit is reached.

x-return-codes.E2: The key is not an Org Admin's or a Developer's.

post.description: Adds an endpoint that Agilis will send events to. **The response includes `secret`, shown only this once:** store it safely and use it to check the `Agilis-Signature` header of every event. Up to 16 endpoints per mode. Org Admin and Developer API keys only; an Advertiser's key is refused (HTTP 403, `E2`). Endpoints belong to the organisation and to your key's mode: a TEST key sees TEST endpoints only.

url.description: Where to send events: an `https://` address with a host name (not an IP address), on the standard port 443, that resolves to a public internet address. Up to 2,048 characters.

enabled_events.description: The event types to send, or `["*"]` for all, including types added later. See [Webhooks](https://www.agilis.dating/api-doc#webhooksSection) for the list.

description.description: Optional. What the endpoint is for, up to 255 characters.

200.description: S1: Endpoint created. It starts receiving events straight away.

secret.description: The signing secret, beginning `whsec_`. Shown only in this response and when rolled.

400.description: E1: Invalid `url`, `enabled_events` or `description`. The `message` says which.

401.description: Invalid or missing API key, or a disabled account. Every bad key gets the same 401.

403.description: E2: The key is not an Org Admin's or a Developer's.

409.description: E4: Your organisation already has 16 endpoints in this mode. Delete one first.

429.description: Rate limit exceeded (60 requests a minute per API key, or repeated invalid keys): wait for the number of seconds in Retry-After.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait. Sent when the per-key limit or the invalid-key limit is reached.

x-return-codes.S1: Endpoint created. It starts receiving events straight away.
x-return-codes.E2: The key is not an Org Admin's or a Developer's.
x-return-codes.E4: Your organisation already has 16 endpoints in this mode. Delete one first.

get.description: One endpoint, without its secret. `failing_since` is when deliveries to it started failing (`null` while they succeed); `disabled_by` is `business` when you turned it off, `system` when Agilis turned it off after 3 days of failures, or `agilis` when Agilis support did.

patch.description: Changes an endpoint. Send only what changes. Turning an endpoint back on (`enabled`) clears its failing state; events that stopped being retried while it was off are not sent again unless you resend them. An endpoint that Agilis support turned off can only be turned back on by Agilis support.

post.description: Replaces an endpoint's signing secret. **The new secret is in the response, shown only this once.** Until `expires_in` passes, every event is signed with both the new and the old secret (two `v1` values in `Agilis-Signature`), so you can update your server without missing any.

parameters.description: The endpoint id. Example: `we_01JD2X4Q7N8P9R0S1T2V3W4X5Y`

expires_in.description: How long the old secret keeps signing. Default `24h`. `now` stops it at once, for a secret that may have leaked.

get.description: Webhook events of the last 30 days in your key's mode, newest first, each with its deliveries to your endpoints. Use it to find events your server missed. Org Admin and Developer API keys only; an Advertiser's key is refused (HTTP 403, `E2`). Endpoints belong to the organisation and to your key's mode: a TEST key sees TEST endpoints only.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Only events of this type.

parameters.name: delivery_success
parameters.description: `false`: only events not yet delivered to every endpoint. `true`: only events delivered everywhere.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Page size, 1 to 100. Default 20.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: The `next_cursor` of the previous page.

200.description: S1: Events returned.

idempotency_key.description: Can be null.

post.description: Sends an event again now, exactly as first sent (same `id`, so your server can recognise a repeat), to one endpoint or to every endpoint it went to. Events can be resent for 15 days. Endpoints that are turned off are skipped.

parameters.name: webhook_event_id
parameters.description: The webhook event id. Example: `whevt_01JD2Y8B3C4D5E6F7G8H9J0K1M`

endpoint_id.description: Send to this endpoint only, including one the event did not go to at first. Omit to send to every endpoint it went to.

401.description: Invalid or missing API key, or a disabled account. Every bad key gets the same 401.

403.description: E2: The key is not an Org Admin's or a Developer's.

404.description: E3: Not found in this organisation and mode (HTTP 404).

409.description: E2: The event is more than 15 days old, is still being sent for the first time, or went to no endpoint (give `endpoint_id`).

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait. Sent when the per-key limit or the invalid-key limit is reached.

post.description:
An Offer was created: paid from your balance at once, or awaiting a card payment.

Sent as an HTTPS POST to each of your endpoints that listens for `offer.created` (or `*`). Verify the `Agilis-Signature` header before trusting the body, and answer with any 2xx within 10 seconds. Ignore an `id` you have already handled: retries and resends repeat it.

parameters.name: Agilis-Signature
parameters.description: `t=<Unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256 of "<t>.<raw body>" with your endpoint secret>`. While a rolled secret is still valid there is one `v1` per secret: accept the message if any matches. Reject a `t` more than 5 minutes from now.

parameters.name: Agilis-Webhook-Id
parameters.description: The webhook event id, the same as `id` in the body.

id.description: Unique id of this webhook event (whevt_…). The same on every retry and resend: use it to ignore duplicates.

created.description: When the change happened, in Unix seconds. Events can arrive out of order: use this to order them.

livemode.description: true for a LIVE endpoint, false for TEST.

test.description: Present and true only on a message sent with Send test event.

object.description: The Offer, in the same shape as an item of GET /offers.

payment_method.description: B: paid from your balance. E: awaiting payment by Stripe link.

amount_charged.description: What was deducted from your balance (payment_method B only).

amount_due.description: What the payment link asks for, before any VAT (payment_method E only).

currency.description: ISO 4217 code of the amounts, your billing currency. Example: GBP

source.description: What caused the change: your API key, the MCP server, the Ad Portal, Agilis, or the system (a scheduled start or end).

idempotency_key.description: The Idempotency-Key of the request that caused it, if any.

object.title: 20% off summer sale
object.description: Discount valid through July
object.push_notification_message: Show this at the till for 20% off everything until the end of July.

200.description: Any 2xx status within 10 seconds means received. The response body is ignored.

default.description: Anything else, a redirect or no answer within 10 seconds is a failed attempt, retried later.

apiKey.name: x-api-key
apiKey.description: Created in the Ad Portal under Manage API Keys. Shown once; Roll key replaces a lost one. One key per mode (TEST or LIVE).

Offer.description: An Offer: a time-limited deal shown to Agilis members near the business, in the mode of the API key that reads it.

advertised_name.description: The business name members see; `null` when your trading name is shown.

push_notification_title.description: The notification members who opted in get when the offer starts. `null` on offers created before these fields existed: those offers are never sent as a notification.

push_notification_message.description: The notification members who opted in get when the offer starts. `null` on offers created before these fields existed: those offers are never sent as a notification.

button_preset.description: The button's text: `claim_offer`, `visit_website`, `install_app`, `book_now`, `get_directions` or `custom`. `claim_offer` on offers created before the button text could be chosen.

button_text.description: Your own button text when `button_preset` is `custom`; otherwise `null`.

image.description: Signed URL of the image. It expires, so do not store it.

gender.description: For example `["Male","Female"]`; empty when the offer targets every gender.

interests.description: `{interest_id, interest_name}` objects; empty when no interest targeting was applied.

offer_status.description: Awaiting Payment, Active, Scheduled, Paused or Ended.

status.description: `enabled` or `disabled`: whether an Admin has disabled the offer.

Event.description: An Event listing shown in the Events tab of the Agilis apps, in the mode of the API key that reads it.

Category.description: An Offer category, or an Event category.

category_id.description: Unique ID of the category. Example: `1`

Interest.description: An interest that an Offer can target.

interest_id.description: Unique ID of the interest. Example: `3`

Page.description: Where a list response is in the whole list: the page size, how many items this page has, and the cursor for the next page.

limit.description: The page size asked for (default 20, at most 100).

count.description: How many items this page has.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` to get the next page; null on the last page.

ReturnCode.description: The body of an error response: a return code, scoped to the endpoint, and a message.

return_code.description: S1/S2 on success, E1–E16 on error. The meaning depends on the endpoint: see its x-return-codes.
